title: Stars streak over La Silla
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars streak across the sky above the telescopes of ESO's La Silla Observatory in this photograph by ESO Photo Ambassador Farid Char. Their light has been drawn out into long arcs.

The arcs record the sky's apparent motion over the night. The stars are not actually moving across the sky; Earth is spinning on its axis, and the camera turns along with it. A long exposure, or a stack of many shorter ones, turns each point of starlight into a curve.

Several of La Silla's telescopes share the scene. In the foreground is the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope. Alongside it are the New Technology Telescope, or NTT, whose mirror is 3.58 metres across, and the ESO 3.6-metre telescope. Far off at the right edge of the frame stands SEST, the Swedish–ESO Submillimetre Telescope, seen only in silhouette.

understand.summary: This is a night-time photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points; a long exposure or stacked exposures are needed to record their motion as trails.

explore: Each telescope at a site like La Silla is built for different kinds of work, which is why observatories often hold a mix of instruments of different sizes and designs.
alt: Star trails across the night sky above several telescopes at La Silla, with the silhouette of a distant telescope far to the right.
